newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA PLANNING FOR DONALD'S FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA PLANNING FOR DONALD'S FUTURE.

text.p: South African cricket bosses are putting together a plan to extend the career of fast bowler Allan Donald.

Donald, and his English wife Tina have been invited to a meeting with convenor of selectors Peter Pollock and United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) managing director Ali Bacher before the third test against India in Johannesburg which starts next Thursday, Bacher said on Friday.
"We are going to have a chat with him and try and work out a way to keep him playing for another five years," he told Reuters.
"He is bowling at his peak now but whereas other fast bowlers are finishing at 31 or 32 we believe Allan can bowl as he is now for five more years."
Donald, 30, has once again demonstrated his fundamental importance to South Africa's international strategy during the current series with India.
He is the leading wicket taker after two tests with 14 scalps to his name and has invariably provided the breakthrough when called upon by skipper Hansie Cronje.

In his 29 tests since South Africa's readmission he has taken 138 wickets to become the second-biggest wicket taker in his country's test history. Only Hugh Tayfield with 170 wickets in 37 tests in the 1950s is ahead of him on the list.
Donald returns to English championship county Warwickshire in 1997, tours England with South Africa in 1998 and is central to his country's plans for the 1999 World Cup also in England.

"We have got various ideas to put to Allan and his wife," Bacher said. "Such as cutting down on his provincial cricket -- for instance he is not playing for his province Free State against India -- securing his financial future, giving him more holidays, things like that."

Donald said on Friday he was looking no further than beyond the 1999 World Cup but added: "I don't know exactly what the meeting will be about but if Doctor Bacher has my health and well-being in mind then that's obviously good news for me."
After the final test against India, South Africa have a home three-test series against Australia.
